claim: Early-modern European trade with Asia was heavily dependent on imported purchasing power in precious metals, much of it ultimately connected to American silver, but the VOC also built profitable intra-Asian trade circuits that generated bullion and reduced its dependence on remittances from Europe.
bounded_by: This is a system-level financing claim. It does not establish that a specific shipment of Ceylon cinnamon was directly purchased with newly mined American silver, nor that American bullion was costless to European empires.
notes: Run41 replaces the intake formulation 'financement américain' with a more precise bullion + intra-Asian trade mechanism.
